source: 人教版2019选择性必修一 Unit 3 同主题阅读(萨雷克国家公园/萨米人与驯鹿/虎豹保护区/西溪湿地/迪士尼乐园/长隆海洋王国)。词限本单元/初中/常见词,答案转述非照抄(不与正文≥5词连续重合),4选项唯一,与完形/听力关不撞。

passages.title: A Summer Where the Sun Never Sleeps
passages.body: I wake up to the sound of the wind hitting the cloth of my tent. Even though the sun is shining brightly, telling whether it is morning or night is impossible. I am above the Arctic Circle, where in summer the sun never sets. Checking my watch, I see that it is half past seven in the morning. I leave my tent and walk over to the mountain edge. Spreading out before me, branches of a river flow through the valley below. I am in the remote far north of Sweden, in a vast park with no roads and no towns. Getting here is quite difficult, so very few people have ever seen this place. To carry all my food and supplies, my bag weighs about thirty kilograms, and the hike over this difficult land is full of sweat and hard work. Yet being in such a beautiful and wild place makes me feel blessed to be alive.

questions.stem: Why is it hard for the writer to tell the time of day?
options: Because the sun does not set there in summer.
Because his watch has stopped working.
Because thick clouds cover the whole sky.
Because the tent has no windows at all.
questions.explanation: 原文 'in summer the sun never sets' 的转述。

questions.stem: What makes the writer's journey so tiring?
options: He has to swim across a wide river.
He must carry all his food and a heavy bag over hard land.
He gets lost on the way many times.
He has to build a new road as he walks.
questions.explanation: 原文 'carry all my food… bag weighs about thirty kilograms… full of sweat and hard work' 的转述。

questions.stem: How does the writer feel about being in this wild place?
options: Lucky and grateful to be there.
Lonely and eager to leave.
Bored by the empty land.
Worried about the cold weather.
questions.explanation: 原文 'makes me feel blessed to be alive' 的转述(感到有幸)。

passages.title: The Sami and Their Reindeer
passages.body: Long ago, the mountains here were covered by huge sheets of ice. About nine thousand years ago this ice melted, leaving behind around a hundred glaciers. Soon after, reindeer began to arrive, and following them came the Sami people, who made this northern territory their home. For hundreds of years, looking after reindeer was a way of life for the Sami. They used the animals' meat for food, their bones for tools, and their skin for making clothes and tents. Because the reindeer were always on the move, the Sami would pick up their tents and travel with them. Today, most Sami have houses in villages and live a modern life, much like their neighbours. Yet every spring a small number of them still follow their reindeer into the valleys, living in tents or old cottages and enjoying their traditions. In 1909 the area became a national park, and now no one but the Sami may live inside it.

questions.stem: What happened after the ice in the mountains melted?
options: The whole area turned into desert.
Reindeer arrived, and the Sami followed them.
A large city was built in the valley.
All the rivers in the region dried up.
questions.explanation: 原文 'reindeer began to arrive… following them came the Sami' 的转述。

questions.stem: How did the Sami traditionally use their reindeer?
options: Only to pull heavy carts of stone.
Mainly to guard their villages at night.
For food, tools, clothes and tents.
Just to sell them to foreign traders.
questions.explanation: 原文 'meat for food, their bones for tools, and their skin for making clothes and tents' 的概括。

questions.stem: What is the situation for most Sami people today?
options: They have left the region forever.
They no longer keep any reindeer.
They are not allowed in the park.
They live a modern life in villages.
questions.explanation: 原文 'most Sami have houses in villages and live a modern life' 的转述。

passages.title: A Home for Tigers and Leopards
passages.topic_cn: 说明·东北虎豹国家公园
passages.body: In northeastern China, a huge new national park was set up to protect Siberian tigers and leopards. The park reaches all the way to the border and joins with wildlife reserves across it. It is nearly four times larger than the old park that once protected these animals. Over the years, growing development in the area had damaged the tigers' homes, and by 1998 it was thought that only six to nine wild Siberian tigers were left in the region. Then, in 2015, a ban on development was put in place. Slowly the numbers began to rise, and the area is now thought to have about thirty-five tigers and seventy leopards. The problem with the old park had been its small size, for these large animals need wide spaces to hunt for food. With a connection to the reserves over the border, the new and far bigger park should give the rare cats the natural room they need to live and grow.

questions.stem: Why were there so few wild Siberian tigers by 1998?
options: Increasing development had damaged their habitat.
They had all moved across the border.
Hunters had been given new licences.
A long drought had dried up the forest.
questions.explanation: 原文 'growing development… had damaged the tigers' homes' 的转述。

questions.stem: What change followed the ban on development in 2015?
options: The tigers left the area completely.
Their numbers slowly started to increase.
The park was made much smaller.
The reserves across the border closed.
questions.explanation: 原文 '… numbers began to rise… about thirty-five tigers and seventy leopards' 的转述。

questions.stem: Why does the new park need to be so large?
options: To make room for many new hotels.
To allow cars to drive freely inside.
Because large cats require broad areas in which to find their prey.
Because the old park had too many visitors.
questions.explanation: 原文 'these large animals need wide spaces to hunt for food' 的转述。

passages.title: The Green Lungs of the City
passages.topic_cn: 说明·西溪国家湿地公园
passages.body: Covering about ten square kilometres in the west of Hangzhou, Xixi is the first national wetland park in China. The way it brings together city life, nature and wetlands makes it a favourite spot for both tourists and local people. At Xixi, taking a boat tour, walking along the paths, and learning about the customs of the old villages are among visitors' best-loved activities. With trees, bushes and colourful flowers growing along the riversides, the park shows a different kind of beauty in each season. When the park was planned, the designers worked hard to limit the impact of people on the land. All the new buildings were made in a traditional fashion so that they would fit into the natural world around them. This green, watery place is home to many birds and fish. With trees growing right in the shallow water, the wetland works as a natural system that cleans water and produces oxygen, which is why people call it the green lungs of the city.

questions.stem: What makes Xixi such a popular place to visit?
options: It has the tallest buildings in Hangzhou.
It is the cheapest park to enter.
It is open only in the summer months.
It blends urban living with nature and marshland in one spot.
questions.explanation: 原文 'brings together city life, nature and wetlands' 的转述。

questions.stem: Why were the new buildings designed in a traditional way?
options: So that they would blend into their natural surroundings.
To attract more shops to the area.
To make the park easier to guard.
Because traditional building was cheaper.
questions.explanation: 原文 '… so that they would fit into the natural world around them' 的转述。

questions.stem: Why is the wetland called the 'green lungs' of the city?
options: Because the trees there are painted green.
Because it cleans water and makes oxygen.
Because it is shaped like a pair of lungs.
Because only green plants may grow there.
questions.explanation: 原文 '… cleans water and produces oxygen…' 的转述。

passages.title: A Magical World at Disneyland
passages.topic_cn: 说明·迪士尼乐园主题公园
passages.body: Of all the theme parks in the world, the one you are probably most familiar with is Disneyland, which can be found in several different countries. A visit to Disneyland brings you into a magical world and makes childhood dreams come true. Travelling through space, visiting a pirate ship, or meeting a lovely cartoon character are all possible here. As you wander around the fantasy park, you may suddenly see a famous character in a parade or even walking along the street. Of course, Disneyland also offers many exciting rides to amuse its guests, from enormous swinging ships to scary free-fall drops that turn your stomach over. There is something for almost every age and taste, so families with small children and groups of older friends can all find rides they love. If you want to have fun and a great deal more than fun, this is surely one park you should not miss.

questions.stem: What does the writer say a visit to Disneyland feels like?
options: Walking through a quiet history museum.
Taking a long and tiring mountain hike.
Entering a magical world where dreams come true.
Studying in a busy science classroom.
questions.explanation: 原文 'brings you into a magical world and makes childhood dreams come true' 的转述。

questions.stem: What might visitors see as they walk around the park?
options: Wild reindeer feeding on the grass.
Workers building new roads everywhere.
Glaciers slowly melting in the sun.
Famous characters in a parade or on the street.
questions.explanation: 原文 '… see a famous character in a parade or even walking along the street' 的转述。

questions.stem: Why does the writer think the park suits many kinds of visitors?
options: Because it offers rides suited to nearly all ages and tastes.
Because tickets there are completely free.
Because it is open all night long.
Because it is found in only one city.
questions.explanation: 原文 '… something for almost every age and taste…' 的转述。

passages.title: Fun by the Sea at the Ocean Kingdom
passages.topic_cn: 说明·长隆海洋王国主题公园
passages.body: In Zhuhai, China, the Ocean Kingdom is one of the leading sea-themed parks in the whole world. Here you can walk under a huge aquarium and watch up to twenty thousand fish swim above your head, including a whale shark many metres in length. Watching the dolphin and sea lion shows is both fun and educational, and you can also see all kinds of interesting animals, even real polar bears. The park has more rides than you can imagine: join a water fight against pirates, get turned upside down on an exciting roller coaster, or get soaked on one of the water rides. Then at night, a splendid parade of lights and a fireworks display fill the sky. If you grow hungry, the park has plenty of restaurants with tasty food for every appetite, and you can even eat while watching the fish swim by. If it is ocean entertainment you are looking for, this park has more than enough to keep you busy all day.

questions.stem: What can visitors do under the huge aquarium?
options: Ride a steam engine through a tunnel.
Look up at as many as twenty thousand fish swimming overhead.
Climb to the top of a glass tower.
Buy and cook their own seafood.
questions.explanation: 原文 'watch up to twenty thousand fish swim above your head' 的转述。

questions.stem: Which of these is offered as one of the park's rides?
options: A quiet boat tour of old villages.
A guided walk to see glaciers.
Joining a pretend battle with pirates in the water.
A class on making iron objects.
questions.explanation: 原文 'join a water fight against pirates' 的转述。

questions.stem: What does the park offer hungry visitors?
options: Only a single small snack bar.
Food brought in from outside.
Free meals for all the children.
Plenty of eateries serving delicious meals to suit any appetite.
questions.explanation: 原文 'plenty of restaurants with tasty food for every appetite' 的转述。
